solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: the word for everything sits inside the word for plant

parts.note: to plant seed is to sow it
everything means all

explanation.surface: A gardener notices that every specimen in a planting looks unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as a noun, a growing thing, but here it is the verb: to put seeds in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A sallow complexion is a yellowish, unhealthy one, so sallow is a synonym of sickly.

definitions.meaning: a dreamy, romantic quality or feeling
... is a famous Hoagy Carmichael standard, and Ziggy ... is a David Bowie persona

explanation.surface: A description of a sentimental ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust names both a dreamy romantic glow and a classic popular song, a pairing of two senses.

clue.text: Invitation to trip that's select and varied

indicators.note: letters that are varied are changed about, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers a choice of holiday tours, exclusive and diverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey but means a dance step, as in 'trip the light fantastic'. Let's Dance is also a David Bowie album and song.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to dance lightly, so a suggestion that we dance is an invitation to trip.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
an instrument that has turned up has appeared, here found sitting inside the scientist's title

explanation.surface: A plant scientist unexpectedly brings along an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' does two jobs: it says the instrument has appeared inside 'geobotanist' (as EOBO), and 'up' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind, an example of a musical instrument.

indicators.note: the contents of a phrase are letters lying inside it, here across the word breaks

explanation.surface: An astronomer lists what is usually found on the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon's' is 'Moon is'; the answer runs through 'typiCAL LIST Of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large Galilean satellites of Jupiter, so it is an example of a moon.

parts.note: ABs, able seamen, are sailors in crosswords
cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: Seamen grumble about how much their levy has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: An abscess is a swelling of pus in body tissue, loosely a growth.

clue.text: Sailormen cavorting with female being other-worldy

indicators.note: sailors cavorting are leaping about, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors frolic with a woman and seem to be in another world.
explanation.walkthrough: Life on Mars? is another David Bowie song, one of several in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Life on Mars would be living things from another planet, beings that are literally extraterrestrial.

definitions.meaning: the ... bar is the long key on a keyboard, and ... is what that bar types
room in the sense of free area or capacity

explanation.surface: Two words naming a drinking lounge in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: With 8 Down it forms Space Oddity, a David Bowie song.
explanation.definitionFit: Space and room are synonyms for empty capacity; the space bar is the keyboard key that types a space.

clue.text: Old German song missing the start creates curiosity

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for German, from Deutschland

indicators.note: the song is missing a letter, so one is removed from it

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

indicators.note: the start of the word 'the' is its first letter

explanation.surface: An old German tune with no opening still makes people curious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the start' is not a generic phrase: it is T, the first letter of 'the', removed from DITTY to leave DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is something strange that arouses interest, so it is a synonym of a curiosity.

indicators.note: the word for winds holds another piece inside it

parts.note: to reel is to wind, as a fishing line, so winds gives reels
the head of the word bridge is its first letter B

explanation.surface: A military report: the resistance keeps a foothold despite the gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridgehead' looks military but gives only its head, B. 'winds' is the verb, not weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The Resistance is a collective name for those who fight an occupier, that is, rebels.

clue.text: Spark, for example, was hot, as user ordered

indicators.note: the words are put in a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: An electrical spark made something hot, as its user wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spark' is Muriel Spark, the Scottish novelist, not an electrical spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Muriel Spark wrote The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie, so she exemplifies a female writer, an old term.

indicators.note: those letters go outside the piece for artist
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word found

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A swindler is discovered lurking outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con artist' looks like the definition, but 'artist' is RA and 'Con' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A con is a swindle, and a fraud is a deception of the same kind: synonyms.

clue.text: Rail disasters affirm dishonesty of leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Train crashes show the railway chiefs have been dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' is not the railway but a dado rail on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado rail is a moulding fixed along a wall at waist height, often simply called a dado.

clue.text: Kind of live appliance returned fast time

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: returned means the appliance word is read backwards

parts.note: an oven is a kitchen appliance
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Asks what sort of live device came back to a fast period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'sort of'; 'Kind' alone is the definition, with 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and benevolent are synonyms, both describing someone well-disposed and generous to others.

clue.text: All spirits left out after spiritual leader's transformations

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the spiritual leader's letter
the leader of spiritual is its first letter

parts.note: each means every one, all individually

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the spirits

parts.note: angels are heavenly spirits

explanation.surface: Spirits are dropped when a guru brings about a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiritual leader' looks like a guru but is just S, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea change is a profound transformation, the phrase from Ariel's song in The Tempest.

indicators.note: the heart of a five-letter word is its middle letter

parts.note: unless means if not

explanation.surface: A lover loses courage unless the room is dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses heart' looks like an idiom for despair but gives the middle letter of 'Loses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunless means without sunlight, so it is a near-synonym of dark or gloomy.

clue.text: Philosopher from the east with hot spice

indicators.note: reading from the east in an across clue means right to left, backwards

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French philosopher
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A thinker from the Orient brings a hot seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' suggests an Eastern sage; it means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumach, also spelt sumac, is a tart red berry ground as a spice in Middle Eastern cooking.

parts.note: convicts chained together breaking rocks are literally linked, not a band with influential friends; a song

explanation.surface: A rock band with friends in high places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock group' suggests a band; here it is prisoners breaking rocks, and 'connected' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of convicts shackled together for hard labour such as rock breaking.

indicators.note: first places the word for about at the front

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a letter in this sense is one who lets property, a leaser

explanation.surface: A letter concerning the first beast that triggers a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is not mail but someone who lets, a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: In animal behaviour a releaser is a sign stimulus that triggers an instinctive response.

indicators.note: the answer is held within the words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: An unusual crochet piece is kept together with a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Velcro is a hook-and-loop strip used to close clothing and bags, a kind of fastener.

parts.note: frank and open both mean candid
a strain is a tune or melody, an air

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank pulls a muscle outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' is a tune, not an injury, and 'Frank' is not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air means taking place outdoors, so it matches outside used as an adjective.

clue.text: Leaves woman's luggage at finishing line

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
a bag is an item of luggage

indicators.note: the finishing letter of line is its last

explanation.surface: A traveller abandons her suitcase at the end of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the plural noun, foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is green leafy vegetation, the leaves and stems of plants used as pasture.

clue.text: Leads injured horse across finishing line

indicators.note: the jumbled horse goes across the final letter, enclosing it
an injured horse is damaged and its letters are knocked into a new order
the finishing letter of line is its last

explanation.surface: A jockey guides a lame mount over the winning post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' makes HEROS from 'horse', and 'across' puts it round the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The leads in a film or play are its principal characters, also called the heroes.

clue.text: Defer settling for a football team's modest ambition

definitions.meaning: to put off settling down for the night
a team that stays up avoids relegation to a lower division

explanation.surface: Two phrases about delays and a club with low hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football the bottom teams of a league drop a division; staying up means avoiding that.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay up means remain out of bed, and in football means keep one's place in a division.

indicators.note: ruins means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An archaeologist dates the pyramids by their ruined state.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron is a pyramid with a triangular base; tetrahedra are such solids.

clue.text: Suspension structure with pieces of rust removed

indicators.note: the letters of rust are removed from the word structure

parts.note: the pieces of the word rust are its four letters, taken in whatever order they occur

explanation.surface: An engineer removes rusty parts from a suspension bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of rust' are the letters R, U, S, T, which 'removed' takes out of STRUCTURE in the order S, T, U, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a suspension of fighting agreed by both sides.

clue.text: Part with cap taken in protest

definitions.meaning: the body part with the kneecap
to take a ... is to kneel in protest

explanation.surface: A cap is removed during a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee carries the kneecap, and 'taking the knee' is kneeling as a gesture against racism.

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a chow is a breed of dog; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone hears a dog's welcome bark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is the Italian informal salutation, used for both hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Inexperienced solver no good to start with

parts.note: the clue speaks to you, the solver

indicators.note: taking each word's first letter gives its start

explanation.surface: A beginner at puzzles was no good at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Young means at an early stage of life, hence lacking experience.

indicators.note: the letters of go are taken away from the economist's term
the remaining letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A political demand to abandon Reagan's economic policy, issued to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking G and O out of REAGANOMICS leaves REAANMICS, which 'ordered' rearranges. Young Americans is a Bowie song.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans are the citizens of the United States, the nation whose policy Reaganomics was.

parts.note: to squash is to press
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A gardener crushes a bloom for pressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river, here the Ure in Yorkshire. Under Pressure is a Bowie song.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure is force exerted on something, so the two are synonyms in the sense of compulsion.

clue.text: She has room in vest at either end

parts.note: to vest is to place or deposit, as is to lodge

indicators.note: the end of the word either is its last letter

explanation.surface: A woman finds space inside her vest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vest' is the verb meaning confer or place, not a garment; 'either end' is the last letter of 'either'. Lodger is a Bowie album.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger rents a room in someone else's home, so she has a room in the house.
